title: Build, test, assemble, release cycle performance and optimisation remediation
objective:
Cut the wall-clock of a release, from the decision to cut to a brew-installable artefact with no hand on the process in between, to the floor set by one honest run per platform, run once, in parallel, and nothing run twice anywhere: locally on this Mac, on kovacs, in CI, and through the assembly, notarisation and packaging stages that follow.

The thread is diagnosis first (hv, 2026-10-31): a root-and-branch review of the release cycle devbin's core gives every project that vendors it, read as built in Devbin, Utilz, Gtools, Intent, Laksa and Conflab, and measured from the record that already exists (CI run history, local seals and run logs, kovacs's logs); no new runs, no code. It records the full Socrates (CTO review) dialog, the measured baseline per project, the places the same work runs more than once, and a remediation plan with options ranked by minutes saved against confidence lost, for hv to choose from. Issue 0295 (a cut with no publish.url tags a commit nothing has tested and re-runs the suite on it) is the first measured instance and is subsumed here.

Fixed points hv named, each of which still has to earn its place on evidence of what it uniquely catches: the kovacs (Ubuntu) run stays, the full CI matrix is green on the exact commit that ships, and a full suite runs on this Mac before the cut asks to confirm. Notarisation happens on this Mac and is a stage of its own. Thorough testing is not the thing being cut; repetition is.

Two criteria every change must meet (hv, 2026-10-31): (a) a general overall reduction in both complexity and time, so a mechanism added to save minutes fails on its face, and a step removed counts twice; and (b) general applicability to all of hv's current and future dev projects, so the answer lands in devbin's core, reaches every project at its next vendor update with nothing per-project to set up, and carries no special case for any one project's shape.

Reach (hv, 2026-10-31): where a project does something bespoke, slow or redundant around the core (its own release driver, pre-push builds, post-cut scripts, derived builds, deploy gates), this thread has the authority to name its remediation, and those remediations are done in the fix phase that follows this diagnosis. The direction follows criterion (b): bespoke machinery retires into the core wherever the core can carry it, and a project keeps only what a config key cannot say.
context:
**Measured baseline, 2026-10-29 to 2026-10-31 (evidence A to E, attached to this thread).** Six projects vendor one release core, byte-identical to Devbin HEAD in all six (0.1.18, source_commit a9b8cd7c). Wall-clock per release, over the release shas: Devbin v0.1.18, 78 min from the last code commit to the public tag (local cut 14.6, publish 56.3 waiting on a candidate matrix whose Ubuntu leg takes 32 to 42 min for the suite this Mac runs in 13 on 8 lanes, macOS 55 to 66, WSL 59; 818 billed-equivalent minutes per candidate, against 126 to 316 for any consumer's release). Gtools v0.8.3, 82 min from candidate to release (the cut 24, of which 9 the suite and 14 holding the terminal for the tag's macOS leg). Utilz 2.14.8, 56 min from candidate to tap, the cut itself under 3 min with notarisation inside it. Intent v3.2.8, 62 min from candidate to tap (kovacs green to release commit 26 to 34 min; post-tag 11 to 19 min of hand-sequenced halves). Conflab v0.6.2, about 5 min from bump to tap, on this Mac, with the bump and the tag pushed before any gate ran. Laksa has no release; its CI job takes 13 to 17 min for a suite that runs locally in 88 s, and its deploy compiles the prod release twice.

**Where the time is.** Not in the core's own steps, which take seconds, and not in runner queues, which are nil across the 95 runs read. It is repetition, in six forms. (1) The suite runs on a candidate and again on its stamped twin, four files and four lines apart, because the gates run after the stamp (ST0007 D38, chosen to avoid a cold rebuild in a worktree) and keep no record ("never already", so a dry run, a stopped cut and the real cut each run the whole suite). (2) Every tag push starts the same workflow twice on one sha, once for the push to main and once for the tag, in two concurrency groups; nine of nine releases in the record. (3) Each leg is serial behind the last by step order rather than data: the snapshot waits for gates, confirm, tag and push though it needs only the tag's commit; formula publish waits for the object step though it needs only the public tag; the ci wait follows the after step; the candidate matrix cannot start until the local suite ends, with a person in between. (4) Devbin's own candidate matrix is an order of magnitude dearer and three times slower than the same suite on this Mac. (5) After the tag, halves that do not depend on each other are sequenced by hand: Intent's macOS assets, Linux assets and tap; Devbin's formula publish, FAILED by construction under --yes, then brew upgrade and the switch. (6) Bespoke project machinery re-runs what it just required or just did: Intent's driver re-runs the five cargo steps and bats after requiring a green kovacs run of the same tree, and its pre-push hook clones and cold-builds the workspace once per remote; Gtools builds gtools-rs in release profile 12 times per release, 10 cold on runners with no cache; Laksa's deploy re-runs credo and the suite CI ran on the same commit, and reads no CI verdict; Conflab runs clippy at the commit and again in pre-flight, keeps three formula writers and calls the oldest. On 2026-10-29 the Devbin suite executed 13 times to ship three patch releases; Gtools's suite 12 times for three.

**What each run has caught (E, the ruling history).** CI Ubuntu: Linux-only reds 0151, 0180, 0223 (v0.1.14's RUSTUP_HOME), 0233 to 0238. kovacs: Intent 3.2.5 and 3.2.6 tags went red on GitHub for Linux-only faults a kovacs run would have found first; since the preflight was made mandatory, 17 runs in a week, 12 green, 5 red, two of them Linux-only cargo-test failures caught before a push; Devbin's K0116 red before the 0.1.16 cut. CI macOS: 0293 (the snapshot's check critic on the macOS job), and the bash 3.2 refusal proof runs nowhere else. WSL: blocks nothing by ruling (ST0008 D50). The local Mac suite: the operator's own pre-cut red runs (2026-10-29 at 06:14, 07:27, 13:04 and 13:14, each before a green cut). No record keyed on a sha exists anywhere in the core; the seal carries platform and run id, never the commit; GitHub's run list, read by ci-state, is the one sha-keyed verdict there is, and the core does not know kovacs exists.

**Constraints the design must respect.** The version lives in the tree (VERSION and sidecars) and is compiled into binaries; release.yml refuses a tag whose name is not VERSION's; the formula's own test asserts the version; a tag is never moved or deleted; the note's date and the generated views are committed; under publish.url the public snapshot is a third sha that no workroom run can stand for; notarisation needs the login keychain on this Mac; kovacs holds no clone and has 2 CPUs (30 min for Devbin's suite against 13 here); the workroom has no GitHub Actions; every project takes the core by vendor update, so the fix is one core change plus each project retiring what the core now carries.

wps.title: Seal records its commit; gates remember a sealed green for (commit, platform)
wps.objective: The seal records its commit and the gates remember. `lib/runlog`: `note_invocation` writes `commit: <sha>` (with the dirty marker when the whole tree holds uncommitted changes, read through `release_tree_state` moved to where runlog can call it, one function) at open, and the seal writes it again at close; runlog gains the one reader of the line. `lib/cmd/release`, gates step: for each declared gate, read `run_all`'s seal ledger for seals on (the release commit R, this platform), every seal clean and green with both commit lines equal, and mark the gate `already`; otherwise run it; the "never already" comment goes. `lib/release.steps`: `release status` reads the same. `docs/releasing.md`, `docs/configuration.md`. `tests/unit` arms: the seal carries the line; a sealed green for R on this platform reads `already`; a seal for another commit does not; a dirty seal never does; an in-flight seal is pending, not green; each seen red first. Serves AC-1.1 and AC-1.2; lands D57 (design.md section 12).

wps.title: The cut reorders and absorbs publish: confirm first, stamp, commit, candidate in every shape, one wait loop, tag on green
wps.objective:
The cut reorders and absorbs publish, in three units. (a) confirm comes first, before any run, and `--yes` answers it and sets the confirmed variable the `after:` commands read; the dry run predicts and runs no gate; the RELEASE seal gains `start:` and `end:` lines (UTC) and one line per leg (name, verdict, sha, duration). (b) the release commit is pushed to `candidate/<tag>` in the no-publish shape too (the publish step's code on the project's GitHub remote); the legs `local` and `candidate` run under one wait loop (`leg_start <leg>`, `leg_read <leg>`; the words are ci-state's, green, failed, pending, none, unknown; poll `ci.poll`, deadline `ci.wait`, default 60m); the tag is made and pushed only on all green; a failed leg or the deadline kills the local runs, deletes the candidate ref and leaves nothing public; the `ci` step and the `ci.tag` and `ci.base` keys leave the schema (the unknown-key refusal stands) and Devbin's `bin/.devbin/config.yaml` drops `ci.tag` in the same unit, keeping `ci.wait: 90m` until WP15 measures; an arm proves the same version is cut again after a failed candidate (`--patch` computes it again, the stamp is `already`, HEAD is the release commit). (c) `release publish` folds into the cut: the snapshot and the public candidate start at the commit step, the publish runs after all green, `--expect` and the separate command retire, object, attach and after follow. Files: `lib/cmd/release`, `lib/release.steps` (step names), `lib/config`, `lib/config.reference.yaml`, `bin/.devbin/config.yaml`, `docs/releasing.md`, `docs/configuration.md`, `tests/unit`. Serves AC-2.1 to AC-2.4; lands D58 to D61 and D63.
 Two lines from dc's WP03 (vc, 2026-10-31): after the flip, `release.ci.workflow` and `release.ci.summary` are read by the `ci-state` command whether or not `ci.query` is declared, so lib/config refuses them only beside a bespoke query; and a release block holding only ci keys passes validation, since Laksa's deploy (WP14) declares `ci.workflow` with no other release key.
 WP01's critic items, taken here or in a WP01b first (vc, 2026-10-31): release_gates_run must not read config inside lib/release.steps (pass the list in from both callers, one read per cut; make the ONE LOOP comment true); status gives a commit row of UNREADABLE its own gates arm; seal_verdict gives the definite void (a green whose tree moved, a tie) its own outcome so status prints pending for it and UNREADABLE only for a failed read; `release gates` reads back release_gates_verdict green naming the seal it just wrote, else exits non-zero; one head reader on both sides of the seal (git_head_identity through git_readonly against bare rev-parse plus release_dirt honouring GIT_DIR); one seal_state for the .errors ladder shared with seal_disagreement_reason; newest_run_stems takes all instead of a fourth kept-run filter; one whole-sha predicate beside git_head_identity.

wps.title: The core ships ci-state; release check refuses a test workflow whose matrix does not fire on candidate/
wps.status_reason: AC-3.1's second half is not on main: release check and the pre-flight do not refuse a test workflow whose matrix does not fire on candidate/ refs (utilz-vc's read of 0332d1a4, verified by vc: no trigger reader in lib/cmd/ci-state or lib/cmd/release, and 76a0fba6's message records no deferral). Remaining scope: a pure reader in ci-state of the workflow's push triggers for candidate/ refs and the failed detail naming the failed jobs or that none ran (dc, after run 3); the reader's two call lines in release check and the cut's pre-flight (cc, with WP02b). The landed half, the ci-state built-in, stands.
wps.objective: The GitHub run reader (`bin/.devbin/cmd/.lib/ci-state`) moves into `lib/` as a built-in and becomes `ci.query`'s default; `ci.query` stays declarable for a project's own reader. It honours the candidate ref and `DEVBIN_RELEASE_TAG` and prints one of green, failed, pending, none, unknown for (repo, sha), the words the wait loop reads verbatim. A workflow checker in the same lib file refuses a test workflow whose matrix does not fire on `candidate/` refs; `release check` and the pre-flight call it (those two call lines in `lib/cmd/release` land after WP02). Devbin's `bin/.devbin/config.yaml` drops its `ci.query` line. `docs/configuration.md`; `tests/unit` (the reader's arms move with it). Serves AC-3.1.

wps.title: Devbin's own workflow: tag trigger and Candidate verdict job removed, lanes from the runner's CPUs, WSL on the candidate
wps.objective:
Devbin's own workflow. Now: `.github/workflows/tests.yml` sets `DEVBIN_TEST_JOBS` on the Ubuntu and macOS jobs from the runner's own CPU count, read in a step, never a written number. After WP02b lands: the tag trigger and the Candidate verdict job (0294) are removed, since the tag is made only on green; WSL stays on the candidate (Q6). The config half (dropping `ci.tag`) is WP02b's; `ci.wait: 90m` stays until WP15 measures the macOS leg under lanes. `docs/releasing.md`'s CI section. Serves AC-4.1; lands D64 and D65.
 Ruled 2026-10-31 (vc, on dc's critic findings): no lanes step; bats-lanes takes `DEVBIN_TEST_JOBS=all`, every CPU `cpu_count` reads (the one probe, issue 0190), refusing when it answers nothing; tests.yml sets `env: DEVBIN_TEST_JOBS: all` on the Ubuntu, macOS and WSL suite steps (WSL's through its WSLENV too) and leaves the run lines untouched; arms hold `all` to `cpu_count`'s own answer and every suite step to the value, no number in any quoting.

wps.title: Remote legs: the release.legs key and runner; kovacs declared in Devbin's config
wps.objective:
Remote legs. `release.legs` names each remote leg (name, host, the gates it runs), and a runner in a lib file of its own drives it: `git push` the release commit over ssh into a bare repo on the host (`~/work/<project>-leg.git`, made if absent), add a worktree at the sha, run the project's own declared gates there under the host's bash (>= 5; kovacs's is `/usr/bin/bash` 5.3.9, no brew bash), copy the seal pair back under `tmp/release/legs/<name>/`, remove the worktree. `command ssh -n`; the remote script goes over `bash -s`, sources `~/.cargo/env`, prepends `$HOME/.cargo/bin` itself and logs `command -v cargo`; detached with its own log; `exit "$rc"` from the gates' status; the Mac side reads the copied seal through WP01's reader, never the ssh exit. `leg_start` and `leg_read` for the loop; the hook-in lands after WP02b. Booking stays outside the core. Devbin's config declares kovacs (`host: kovacs`, this Mac's ssh alias for matts@10.211.55.3). `lib/config` (the key), `docs/configuration.md`, `bin/.devbin/config.yaml`, `tests/unit`. Serves AC-3.2; lands D62.
 Ruled 2026-10-31 (vc, on dc's four questions): `release.legs` is a list of ssh host aliases (`legs: [kovacs]`), the entry the leg's name, validation holding it to a plain alias; the bare repo's path and the copy-back directory are recipe from the project name and the alias; R reaches the host by `git send-pack` into `refs/devbin/legs/<R>` (plumbing, no pre-push hook: nothing public moves; `--no-verify` stays banned and this is not it); a mechanism failure reads `unknown` with its reason; the host carries what the declared gates need (kovacs has Intent 3.2.8; the rest of the census asked of kovacs-sysadm), and a gate that cannot run there is the leg's `failed`.

wps.title: The macOS stage at the release commit, as a leg
wps.objective:
The macOS stage at the release commit. `lib/cmd/macos`: `app-sign` and `app-notarize` require HEAD to be the release commit, not the tag; the stage runs as a leg of the cut (`leg_start`, `leg_read`; the hook-in lands after WP02b); `publish` is unchanged and follows the object. `docs/configuration.md`. No project in this repository declares `macos:`, so the suite's arms are the floor and the first Utilz or Intent cut in the new shape is the acceptance run (D66). Serves AC-3.3.
 Ruled 2026-10-31 (vc, on dc's reading of lib/cmd/macos): `app-sign`'s precondition is a clean tree and HEAD at the tag's commit when the tag exists, else at the release commit (the untagged commit whose VERSION is the version being released); `app-sign` records HEAD's full sha in the stage; `publish` refuses a stage recorded at another commit than the tag's, and one with no record as unknown provenance; the commit-stamp check reads the release's commit, the tag's when it exists and HEAD before it; `app-notarize` leaves the tie to `publish`. Arms on macOS with Apple's tools stubbed, each red first.

wps.title: Attach reads the candidate run: assets keyed on the release commit's sha
wps.objective: Attach reads the candidate run. `lib/release.steps`: `release_read_assets_run` is keyed on the release commit's sha, so the assets workflow's run on the candidate is the one read; `lib/cmd/release`: attach is a step of the cut after the object, in parallel over disjoint files with the macOS publish. `docs/releasing.md`. No assets workflow exists in this repository, so the first Intent cut in the new shape is the acceptance run (D66). Serves AC-3.3.

wps.title: Formula under the yes; assets mode with the cask verified
wps.objective:
The formula under the yes. `lib/cmd/formula`: `publish` is confirmed by the cut's yes (the confirmed variable `--yes` sets), so a `--yes` cut publishes the tap and no `after:` step fails for want of a person; the assets-mode cask render is verified, or added where the built-in lacks it. `lib/cmd/release`: the `after:` commands run under the yes. `docs/releasing.md`. Serves AC-2.1 and AC-3.3; lands D58.
 Carries issue 0296 (filed 2026-10-31): `lib/cmd/formula:548` and `:665` pass no remote to `release_repo`, so with `remotes:` declared and no `repo:` the formula reads origin's repository where the cut and `ci-state` read the first declared remote's; the fix is `cfg_release_first_remote` at both call sites.

wps.title: A Devbin release through the new shape, then the vendor sweep into the five consumers
wps.objective:
hv's to go (directive 3). A Devbin release carrying WP01 to WP08 cut through the new shape itself, the first measurement: the RELEASE seal's start, end and per-leg lines go on this thread beside design.md's expected column. wps.title: Measure and re-read: RELEASE seal clock lines against the expected column; kovacs, lanes, the consumers' macOS legs
wps.objective: Measure and re-read, after the first release of each project in the new shape: the RELEASE seal's clock lines against design.md section 5's expected column; the kovacs leg's duration and what it caught beside the candidate's Ubuntu leg (Q4, re-read after a few releases); Devbin's macOS leg under lanes, and whether `ci.wait: 90m` can drop to the 60m default (Q5); the consumers' macOS legs against their critical path (Q12). wps.title: Build artefacts cached by the hash of their inputs: nothing rebuilt that a recorded input hash already built (D67)
wps.objective: hv's direction (2026-10-31, D67): as CI, CD and assembly tools keep a registry or catalogue of built artefacts keyed on the commit they were built from, devbin's core caches build artefacts by the hash of their inputs, so that while nothing in the assembled dependencies has changed the artefact is pulled by its hash rather than rebuilt. Design first, then code: (1) measure, from the record, which builds repeat per release and what each one's inputs are (Gtools's twelve release-profile builds of gtools-rs, ten cold on runners; Intent's pair built at the tag and again by its pre-push hook's cold clone; Laksa's prod `mix release` twice; Conflab's three cargo builds and its xcodebuild), using each project's existing build-input scope where one exists (Intent's pre-push currency check, issue 0518); (2) shape the key as the tree hashes of the declared build-input paths at the commit (`git rev-parse <commit>:<path>` over `project.build_inputs`), never the commit alone; (3) shape the registry: a cache directory on the machine for local builds, the runner's cache or the release's own assets on CI, each entry the artefact plus the key and the toolchain it was built with; (4) `bin/devbin build` consults the registry before building and records after, and `release attach` may take an artefact from it; (5) one core mechanism with one `build_inputs` fact per project, nothing else per project (criterion b). Serves the thread's objective (nothing built twice); ACs to be minted with the design.

wps.title: A gate declares the platforms it runs on: inactive elsewhere, never failed (D69)
wps.objective:
A gate declares where it is meant to run, once, at the gate, and a host elsewhere counts it inactive rather than failing its leg (D69, design.md s12; amends D62's last clause). Scope S, dc's lane, after WP05 lands with run 3 and before WP09's cut: 0.1.19 carries it because Gtools's kovacs leg (WP11) stops at `bin/gtools app test --unsigned` without it, the one macOS-only gate in any consumer's `test all`.

Build: `platforms:` as a list under `commands.<cmd>.options.<opt>` (lib/config's two option-key sites, lib/config.reference.yaml, docs/configuration.md's option table and its `all` paragraph, lib/pages/test.md and check.md beside `in_all`); one derivation of this host's platform word (`macos`, `linux`, from `uname -s`) in lib/helpers, reusing WP01's if D57's (commit, platform) record already keys on a word, new otherwise with D57's key then reading from it, never a second spelling; `option_active` (lib/resolve) refuses an option whose list omits this host's word, `option_unavailable_reason` and `help --why` name the reason, the by-name dispatch refuses through the existing inactive route with it, and the `all` count line counts it; a list value outside the words is refused at config read, naming key and value. `in_all: false` is untouched. AC-6.1 and AC-6.2 are this package's; AC-6.3 (the plan's pre-flight refusal of a gate active on no leg the cut will run) is cc's inside WP02b when legs enter the plan, reading this same predicate against each leg's probed platform.

Evidence (the slim list): arms red on main then green under BSD and GNU for `all` with a foreign platform (inactive, counted, named), with this platform (runs), without `platforms:` (runs); the by-name refusal with its reason; a bad value refused at config read; `help --why`'s line; one targeted run with the tree scans and help, shellcheck, critic once, booked through the desk. Not here: Gtools's config (WP11), knowledge of CI's platforms, any per-leg list (D62 stands).

wps.title: docs/assembly-and-the-build-cache.md: Devbin's Build Cache for Optimised Release Assembly, design and tech note plus how-to
wps.objective:
`docs/assembly-and-the-build-cache.md`: "Devbin's Build Cache for Optimised Release Assembly", a detailed design and tech note plus how-to. hv, 2026-10-31 (in vc's session, during the fix phase): "I want to add in a task to do (not now, but right at the end when this is all landed) ... Let's not forget about that." Written LAST, after WP01 to WP17 and the consumer packages WP10 to WP14 have landed and WP15 has measured, from the as-built and never from the plan.

Contents: why (D67, the repeats table in design.md s13: what was built or tested twice before, with WP15's measurements); the key (sha256 over the declared `build.inputs` at the commit plus toolchain and platform lines) and what it is durable against; the registry (D68: `DEVBIN_CACHE_HOME`, the XDG default, one directory per project and per artefact, `manifest.yaml` and `SHA256SUMS` as provenance); the verbs (`bin/devbin cache key/get/put/list/rm/gc`) and the `build:` block; how a cut assembles a release from cached artefacts, what it rebuilds and what it never pulls (a doubtful entry); the miss-never-failure rule (AC-5.5: unset, empty, absent or unusable root) and what doctor reports; integrity; what it removed from each consumer. How-to: a maintainer declaring inputs, reading a hit, clearing an entry, running gc, moving the root; a new consumer adopting it. critic-prose once; no manual wrapping; indexed wherever docs/ are listed (README's docs table if there is one).

criteria.text: Every sealed run's invocation block records the commit the run stood on, as a commit: line, with the dirty marker when the tree held uncommitted changes.
The cut's gates step marks a gate already when a sealed green for the release commit on this platform exists, and runs it otherwise; the never-already rule is gone.
The cut asks its one yes before any gate or leg runs, naming the tag, the release commit, every remote, the object, the assets and the tap; --yes answers it and the after: commands run under it.

After the stamp and commit, every leg (the local gates, the candidate matrix, each declared remote leg, the macOS stage where declared) starts together and is read by one wait loop; the tag is made and pushed only when every leg is green, and a red or a timeout leaves no tag and nothing public.

In every shape the commit the matrix tests is pushed to candidate/<tag> before its run is read, and the candidate ref is deleted once the tag is pushed or the cut stops red; the same version may be cut again while no tag exists.
release publish, --expect, the ci step and the ci.tag and ci.base keys are retired; the dry run runs no gate; ci.wait defaults to 60m; the RELEASE seal carries start and end clock lines.

The core ships the GitHub run reader as a built-in, honouring the candidate ref and DEVBIN_RELEASE_TAG; release check and the pre-flight refuse a test workflow whose matrix does not fire on candidate/ refs.
release.legs runs each declared remote leg at the release commit's sha on its host and reads its seal back through the same reader; Devbin declares kovacs.
The macOS stage signs and notarises at the release commit as a leg; attach reads the assets run by the release commit's sha; the formula publishes under the cut's yes.
The first Utilz or Intent cut in the new shape signs and notarises at the release commit as a leg (D66), as that cut's RELEASE seal records; satisfied by evidence from that seal.

Devbin's test workflow runs each leg once per sha on the candidate: no tag trigger, no Candidate verdict job, lanes from the runner's own CPU count, WSL on the candidate. The push step's fast-forward of public main to the snapshot runs Ubuntu again on that sha, main's own check of the published branch, which the cut does not wait for (amended on hv's TUI answer in vc's window, 2026-11-01 18:43Z by date -u).

criteria.text: Utilz, Gtools, Intent, Conflab and Laksa each retire the bespoke machinery design.md section 7 names, or carry it only as a config key, and their test workflows fire on candidate/ and not on tags.

cache key prints one key for two commits that differ only outside the declared build inputs, a different key when an input's object changes, and refuses a dirty input path with a line and exit 7, the cache's own code in devbin's exit-code contract (WP16, D67; exit 7 by vc's decision 113).
A second build on the same key builds nothing: the record says 'pulled <artefact> <key>' and the artefact's bytes are the first build's; a dirty tree builds and cache put records nothing (WP16).
A registry entry whose SHA256SUMS or manifest key does not verify is refused, removed with a line, and the build runs (WP16).
The first consumer cut after adoption shows WP15's builds-per-release count below its baseline for every project with a build: block, by project (WP16).

With DEVBIN_CACHE_HOME unset or empty the cache root is the XDG default; with no registry there, cache get is a miss (exit 1), the build runs and cache put makes the root and the entry; with an unusable root (a relative value, a file, an unwritable directory) get and put each say so once with exit 7, and the build's own exit is unchanged (WP16, D68; exit 7 by vc's decision 113).

An option declaring platforms: that omits this host's platform word is inactive on <cmd> all: counted on the count line, named by help --why with its reason (the platforms it runs on and this host's), and refused with the same reason when run by name; with this host's word listed, or with no platforms: key, it runs as before.
A platforms: value outside the core's platform words is refused at config read, naming the key and the value, as an unknown key is.

The cut's plan refuses at pre-flight a gate in all that is active on none of the legs the cut will run, local and remote, naming the gate and its platforms, before any gate runs; a gate active on at least one leg passes the check (lands with WP02b).

# ST0011 design: the release cycle, diagnosed and remediated

Diagnosis phase, 2026-10-31, by vc on hv's order. Evidence A to E, the Socrates brief and the full Socrates dialog are attached to this thread; every number below names its source there. No code was written in this phase. This document is the thread's design record: the diagnosis, the recommendation, the ranked options, the per-project remediations and the fix-phase work packages. The argument behind each is in `socrates-dialog.md`; this document does not repeat it.

## 1. The question and the rulings

A release of any project that vendors devbin's release core takes an hour or more, and the same suite runs several times per release. hv's rulings (the thread's objective): the target is the floor, one honest run per platform, run once, in parallel, nothing run twice; kovacs, the full CI matrix on the shipping commit and a local Mac suite each stay unless the evidence shows a run catches nothing another does not; notarisation stays on this Mac; every change reduces both complexity and time (criterion a) and lands in the core for every present and future project (criterion b); bespoke project machinery is in reach and retires into the core where the core can carry it.

## 3. Diagnosis: six repetitions, each with its mechanism

1. **The suite runs on the candidate and again on its stamped twin.** The core stamps, commits, then gates on the release commit (`lib/release.steps:94`; `lib/cmd/release:1034-1038`, "never already"); the release commit differs from the candidate by the version string, a date and two regenerated views (A s3.1; Gtools v0.8.3 `git show --stat`: 4 files, 4 lines). Every pre-cut run (hand `test all`, kovacs, gyges, a dispatched CI run, a dry run that runs the gates for real) is therefore a verdict on a tree that never ships, and the cut runs the suite again. The gates step records nothing, so a stopped cut re-runs it whole on resume (Gtools 0.8.0 and 0.8.1, C Gtools s1). Chosen by ST0007 D38 to avoid a cold rebuild in a worktree (E s4): a cost ruling, not a confidence one.
2. **Every tag push starts the same workflow twice on one sha.** The push step pushes the release commit to main and then the tag seconds apart (`lib/cmd/release:1155,1162`); each project's workflow keys concurrency on workflow, event and ref, so the push-to-main run and the tag run both live, and their Ubuntu legs are identical work: nine of nine releases in the record, Intent doubling two workflows (D fact 1 and 2). The macOS legs are not doubled inside the pair only because they are conditioned on the tag ref.
3. **Serial by step order, not by data.** A s5 names fourteen waits; the ones that cost minutes: the snapshot and candidate push wait for gates, confirm, tag and push though `snapshot_build` needs only the tag's commit and the public tip (so Devbin's 13-minute local suite and 47-minute matrix never overlap); `formula publish` waits for the object step's poll of a workflow that takes seconds though it needs only the public tag; the `ci` wait follows the `after` step; every GitHub wait is a 15 s poll with no overlap between waits; the `macos` built-in cannot start until HEAD is the tag.
4. **Devbin's own matrix is the outlier, by arithmetic.** 818 billed-equivalent minutes per candidate against 126 to 316 for a consumer's release and 14 for Conflab; its Ubuntu leg takes 32 to 42 min and its macOS leg 55 to 66 for a suite this Mac runs in 13 on 8 lanes (D fact 8). The cause: `bats-lanes` runs the parallel lane at half the CPUs and never below two (`bin/.devbin/cmd/.lib/bats-lanes:35-36,67`), which is 8 lanes on this 16-CPU Mac and 2 on `ubuntu-latest` (4 vCPU) and `macos-latest` (3 vCPU); the file's own header records 40.6 min serial here against 39.5 on CI's two-CPU runner (`:11`). One red leg costs a whole new version (v0.1.17 to v0.1.18, A s0).
5. **Hand-sequenced halves after the tag.** Intent: macOS assets, Linux assets and the tap are three independent halves run as five commands, 11 to 19 min (B B1). Devbin: `release publish --yes` always ends with the formula step FAILED because `--yes` is no person's yes for the tap (`lib/cmd/release:1484-1486`; A s7), then `brew upgrade` and `devbin use brew` by hand. Lights out is not possible on the current shape for any project.
6. **Bespoke machinery re-runs what it just required.** Intent's 1524-line driver gates on the candidate (the order 0295 asks the core for), yet re-runs the five cargo steps and bats it required a green kovacs run of on the same tree, in a private empty-target worktree (cold every cut), and its pre-push hook clones and cold-builds the workspace once per remote (B B5). Gtools builds gtools-rs in release profile 12 times per release, 10 cold on runners with no cargo cache (C Gtools s2). Laksa's deploy re-runs credo and the suite CI ran on the same commit and reads no CI verdict; the crate's tests run twice per `test all` (C Laksa s2). Conflab's own release pushes the bump and the tag before any gate, runs clippy at the commit and again in pre-flight, and keeps three formula writers (C Conflab s6 and s7). Utilz's `tools/ci-state` ignores `DEVBIN_RELEASE_TAG` and its 2.14.8 release log never sealed (B A7, E s2).

Common root: **no verdict is keyed on a sha, and no step reads one.** The seal records platform and run id, never the commit (`lib/runlog:402,406`); the only sha-keyed record is GitHub's run list, read by `ci-state`; kovacs's verdicts live in summary files the core never sees; so every step that wants confidence runs the suite itself. hv's "remember the hash that worked and tag it" is answered by an ordering plus that one memory: make the commit that ships first, test it once everywhere at the same time, record each verdict against its sha in the seal that already exists, tag it when all are green (dialog, phase 1 and phase 5).

## 5. The recommended shape

One command from the yes to the brew-installable artefact (dialog section 1 has each step's sources):

1. **resolve, pre-flight** (this Mac, reads only), minus the `ci.base` read; plus a refusal of a test workflow whose matrix does not fire on `candidate/` refs.
2. **confirm**: the one yes, before anything runs, naming the tag, the release commit the stamp will make, every remote, the object, the assets and the tap; its meaning is "ship if every leg is green"; `--yes` says it and sets the confirmed variable the `after:` commands read.
3. **stamp, commit** (seconds; unchanged in content).
4. **legs, started together, one wait loop**, a red or a timeout in any leg stopping with nothing public: (a) the candidate: the release commit pushed to `candidate/<tag>` on the project's remote, or for the publish shape the snapshot of its tree pushed to the public candidate, the moment the release commit exists; the matrix runs there; (b) the local gates in place on the release commit, each seal recording the commit, the step `already` when a sealed green exists for this commit on this platform; (c) remote legs the config names (kovacs): clone at the sha, run, copy the seal back, the same reader; (d) the macOS stage where declared: sign and notarise at the release commit, not the tag.
5. **tag, push** on all green; candidate ref deleted; publish shape fast-forwards the public main and pushes the lightweight tag at the snapshot.
6. **object** (`gh release create`, or `release.yml`'s run).
7. **assets**, in parallel over disjoint files: `attach` reads the assets workflow's run by the release commit's sha (the candidate run); `macos publish` uploads the staged copy; sums last.
8. **the tap**: `formula publish` under the yes from step 2; source mode as soon as the tag is public, assets mode after the sums.
9. **end**: the brew switch note; `brew upgrade` and `use brew` on each machine remain the person's.

Expected wall-clock from the yes to the tap, the longest leg plus a measured tail of about a minute (dialog section 1 table): **Devbin about 57 (today 71 to 78), Gtools about 15 (cut 23.8; candidate to release 82), Utilz about 15 (56), Intent about 21 (62), Conflab about 9 (5 today, with the tag pushed before any gate), Laksa's deploy stops re-running the suite and the prod compile.** Every figure is a measured leg plus a minute; the first release in the new shape is the measurement, which is why the RELEASE seal gains start and end clock lines (today no log carries one, A s8).

**Measured at devbin 0.1.19, the first release in the new shape** (WP15's first read, 2026-11-01, from the RELEASE seal `tmp/release/20261101-2050.RELEASE.out`, run 9938a615). Its clock lines read `start: 2026-11-01T20:50:29Z` and `end: 2026-11-01T21:53:56Z`, with one line per leg: `candidate green 0b5e4fa0f540 3743s run 41348944891`, `local green e532a0f67250 1065s` and `legs.kovacs green e532a0f67250 3326s`. The yes fell between the prompt (20:50:29Z) and the release commit (20:50:40Z), and the tap's commit is 21:53:50Z: **about 63 minutes from the yes to the tap, against about 57 expected and 71 to 78 at v0.1.18.** The longest leg was CI's macOS job, 61.9 minutes (20:51:00Z to 21:52:54Z), its `test all` under 3 lanes taking 61.4 of them; v0.1.18's was 55.3. Ubuntu took 23.1 minutes under 4 lanes (31.8 at v0.1.18), and WSL 2 took 37.5 (59.1), red on one arm, filed as 0318, which blocks nothing by design. The tail from macOS's end to the tap was 56 seconds, the expected minute. The kovacs leg, read against the candidate's Ubuntu leg, took 55.3 minutes on 2 CPUs (its seal's start 20:50:56Z, end 21:46:12Z: check all, test all and doctor), 2.4 times Ubuntu's, and ended 6.7 minutes before macOS, so it was not the critical path; its lint ran clean, with no OOM kill. The local gates took 17.8 minutes. The first cut that evening, run 321d95b0, stopped red at the legs step at 20:30:38Z on 0317's arm, and is not this measurement.

What it removes from the core: `release publish` as a separate command with its second pre-flight and confirm; `--expect`; the `ci` step and the `ci.tag` and `ci.base` keys; the gates step's "never already" rule; the dry run's real gates; the prompted-only confirmed variable; the tag-at-HEAD precondition in `macos`; the Candidate verdict job and the `tags:` trigger on the test workflow; three step names. What it adds: one `commit:` header line in the seal and one reader; the candidate push in the no-publish shape (the publish step's code on another remote); a `release.legs` key and its runner; the attach keyed on sha; a built-in `ci-state`; `after:` running under `--yes`; clock lines in the RELEASE seal. From the projects it removes Intent's driver, two preflight scripts, a hook's build path and five hand steps; Utilz's three tools; Gtools's reader and wait; Conflab's release handler, two formula writers and a workflow skipped since v0.5.7; Laksa's double suite run and local prod compile; three copies of one `ci-state` (dialog, phase 3 ledger).

### 5.1 vc's assessment of the recommendation

I adopt the dialog's recommendation with four notes.

1. **The one real addition is `release.legs`**, the core driving a run on another machine over ssh. The dialog flags it and names the degraded form (the desk runs the leg, the core reads the copied seal). I agree it passes criterion (a) on the estate's ledger: three bespoke copies of the same thing (Intent's `preflight-linux.sh` and `preflight.lib`, Devbin's K-orders, Gtools's hand run) retire for one shipped runner, and without it the kovacs fixed point and lights out contradict each other. It is hv's to accept (question 4).
2. **Lanes alone will not bring Devbin's macOS leg far.** Setting `DEVBIN_TEST_JOBS` to the runner's CPUs gives 4 lanes on `ubuntu-latest` and 3 on `macos-latest`, not 8; the scaling point on record is 2 lanes at 30 min against 8 at 13, so expect the leg to roughly halve, not quarter. The next lever is parallelism by job count: shard the bats suite across N runner jobs, each a subset of files, with one summary. That is a mechanism, bats-specific, and it belongs after the first measurement, not before. Larger runners are the third lever and cost money on a repository whose minutes are otherwise free.
3. **The dialog is right to keep CI macOS whole for the consumers** on the ground that it is not the longest leg under the parallel shape, and right that Devbin's cannot shrink because its CI tests the snapshot. I would add one line to the expected table: the Gtools and Utilz kovacs legs are not on record and may be the longest leg for those two; if so, the kovacs question (4) decides their floor.
4. **Decisions 32 and 81 stand unchanged** under this shape: release candidates run the whole matrix, and macOS and WSL run only on candidates, tags and dispatch. The shape makes the candidate ref the one place the matrix runs, which is what both rulings asked for.

## 6. The options, ranked

The dialog's full table (section 2 there, twenty rows with sources, complexity counts and the two criteria) is the record. Condensed:

| # | option | minutes per release | (a) | (b) | needs |

## 11. The leg contract

vc's ruling, 2026-10-31; cc and dc build to it, and a question about it comes to vc rather than a second draft.

- **R** is the release commit the stamp step makes; every verdict is keyed on R's sha and a platform. The tested sha is R, pushed to `candidate/<tag>` on the project's GitHub remote, or under `publish.url` the snapshot S of R's tree; the RELEASE seal records R and S.
- **A leg yields one word, `ci-state`'s, verbatim**: `green`, `failed`, `pending`, `none` (no record, or not started), `unknown` (could not read, with its reason printed). The legs: `local` (the declared gates in place at R on this machine; its verdict is the seal pair with `commit: R` and `platform:` this one, `.errors` empty and not in flight); `candidate` (the matrix on `candidate/<tag>`, read by `ci.query`, whose default is the built-in reader, for the tested sha; Test Summary's verdict; WSL blocks nothing, D50); `legs.<name>` (a remote host runs the project's own declared gates at R in a worktree of a bare repo on that host; the seal pair is copied back under `tmp/release/legs/<name>/` and read by the same reader); `macos` (sign and notarise at R, where declared; its own seal).
- **Order**: resolve, pre-flight, confirm (the one yes, before anything runs; `--yes` answers it and sets the confirmed variable the `after:` commands read; the yes names the tag, R, every remote, the object, the assets and the tap), stamp, commit, then every leg starts in one step and one loop reads them all; tag and push only when every leg is green; then object, attach, after (the formula under the yes).
- **Already**: before a leg starts, its verdict for (sha, platform) is read; a recorded green is `already` and the leg is not started. The gates keep no other memory. A seal is remembered only when its commit line at open and at close agree and both are clean.
- **The loop**: poll every `ci.poll` seconds (15 today), deadline `ci.wait` (default 60m) from the loop's start, one GitHub read per poll, one line per state change with the clock. End: all green, tag; any `failed`, stop; the deadline, stop as a timeout. On a stop the local background runs are killed, remote legs are left to finish (their seals are records), the candidate ref is deleted and nothing is public; R stays in local history, the fix lands on top and the same version is cut again while no tag exists (Q3).
- **Interface**: the loop (cc, WP02b) calls `leg_start <leg>` and `leg_read <leg>` (one word plus a detail line) per leg; cc owns the loop and the `local` and `candidate` legs; dc owns `legs.<name>` (WP05) and `macos` (WP06) behind the same pair, in files of their own, with one-arm hook-ins landing after WP02b. Every verdict goes through the seal reader (WP01) or `ci.query`; nothing else reads one.
- **Clock**: the RELEASE seal gains `start:` and `end:` lines (UTC) and one line per leg: name, verdict, sha, duration.
- **Booking is outside the core**: the operator or the coordinating node books the box before the cut; the core never calls `intent estate`.
- **A failure of the mechanism** (ssh or `gh` unreachable) reads as `unknown` with its reason printed and counts as not green; at the deadline it is a timeout. No silent errors.

## 13. The artefact cache (WP16, D67, D68)

vc's design, 2026-10-31, on hv's direction. Design first: the core verbs land in Devbin after the fix-phase runs (dc's lane, after WP06a), and each consumer adopts in its WP10 to WP14 commit. Nothing here changes a fix-phase unit.

**What repeats today.** From the record (sections 3 and 6 of the dialog): Gtools builds gtools-rs at the release profile twelve times per release, ten of them cold on runners; Intent builds its pair at the tag and again in its pre-push hook's cold clone; Laksa compiles its prod `mix release` twice per deploy; Conflab runs three cargo builds and one xcodebuild. The inventories asked of the five consumer estates on 2026-10-31 (the pre-sweep brief, item 1) confirm each row with its trigger, its platform and whether it is cold before the verbs are cut. Devbin itself builds nothing: its suite is a gate, and D57's GATES seal is that gate's cache.

**The key.** An artefact's key is the sha256 of the sorted lines `<path>\t<object id>` over the declared input paths at a commit, the object id being `git rev-parse <commit>:<path>` (a tree id for a directory, a blob id for a file), plus three lines, `toolchain\t<id>`, `platform\t<word>` and `arch\t<word>`. Tree ids and not the commit, because a commit that changes only docs, the whiteboard or `intent/` leaves every input id as it was, so the key stands and the artefact is pulled: that is the whole saving on a re-cut after a red leg (the fix lands, R changes, the inputs mostly do not) and on Intent's cold clone, whose commit carries the same ids. Git's ids and not a content hash of the files, because git has hashed them already, `rev-parse <commit>:<path>` reads an object with no checkout, so R's key exists before any worktree is made for it, and the key is identical in every clone. The toolchain, because the same inputs under another compiler are another artefact; its id is the tool's own version line (`cargo --version`; from `elixir --version`, the Erlang/OTP release and its erts with Elixir's own line, leaving out the emulator's flags, which follow the host's CPU count and `ERL_FLAGS` and not what a build makes; `xcodebuild -version`; `swift --version`), read by the core from a built-in table keyed on the artefact's tool word, so no project writes a version anywhere, and asked where the build runs, cargo in `project.cargo_root`, where rustup reads a `rust-toolchain` file, and every other tool at the project root, so the key never depends on where the command was run. The platform, because a built artefact is for one, as this host's platform word, `macos` or `linux` (`platform_word` in lib/helpers, vc's decision 108); the seals' `platform:` line stays an identity of its own, the OS build and the bash a run stood on, and is not the key's word. The architecture, because one platform and one toolchain build another artefact for another CPU: x86_64 and arm64 runners would otherwise share a key, and an arm64 job would pull an x86_64 binary; the key names the word `uname -m` gives (`platform_arch` in lib/helpers, hv's decision 115). A dirty tree has no key: an input path with uncommitted changes is no commit's object, so the build runs and nothing is recorded, as `git_head_identity`'s `+dirty` refuses a confident sha. A key is printed whole in every record, never cut.

**The declaration**, one block per project in `bin/.devbin/config.yaml`, which is criterion (b):

```yaml
build:
  inputs:
    - Cargo.toml
    - Cargo.lock
    - src
    - crates
  artefacts:
    gtools:
      tool: cargo
      path: target/release/gtools
    gtools-app:
      tool: xcodebuild
      path: build/Release/Gtools.app
      inputs:
        - Cargo.toml
        - Cargo.lock
        - src
        - macos
```

In block form, since devbin's config parser refuses YAML's flow collections (`[...]` and `{...}`). `build.inputs` is the one fact; an artefact's own `inputs:` narrows it where that artefact reads fewer paths. `tool` names the toolchain table's row; `path` is what the project's `build` handler writes, read after a build and written back at a pull. lib/config's key schema carries the block's keys, as an arm of `_cfg_path_known` like the `worktrees:` block's, with the one reader of its input paths (`cfg_build_input_paths`), which the cache, doctor and validation share, so config validation refuses an unknown key, a tool word outside the table, an artefact's name that does not start with a letter or a digit (`is_artefact_name` in lib/helpers), a declared path that is empty, absolute, holds an empty, `.` or `..` segment, or lies in `.git` in any case of its letters (`cache_path_problem`), and an artefact's path that is, holds or lies in any input path the block declares, in any case of their letters (`cache_paths_overlap`), since a pull replaces what is at the path, so a pull never writes or removes anything outside the project or over it, nor an input's working tree, and one path never makes two keys; `get` refuses a path the repository tracks files at, in any case of its letters; and doctor fails an input path the block declares that HEAD does not hold.

**The registry** (hv's ruling, 2026-10-31 10:5xZ, D68). Its root is `DEVBIN_CACHE_HOME`, an environment variable, so the cache lives wherever a machine puts it; unset, the core uses `$(xdg_dir cache)/devbin`, and hv's fleet sets it to `/Users/matts/Devel/.cache` through Molt, a path no shipped file names. Under the root, one directory per project, and under that one per artefact keyed by the input hash: `<root>/<project>/<artefact>/<key>/`, holding the artefact (a file, or a tar of a directory's contents, so a pull writes them at the path the declaration names then), `manifest.yaml`, the artefact's provenance (project, artefact, the key and each of its lines, the commit the build ran at and its tree's cleanliness, the toolchain id, the platform, the architecture, the host, the clock in UTC, the size, the artefact's sha256), and `SHA256SUMS`. YAML because the core already reads it (`bin/.devbin/config.yaml`) and a person can read it too. One registry per machine, since an artefact is for its platform: kovacs and gyges keep their own, and the remote-leg runner (D62) copies seals back, never artefacts. On CI, the runner's cache under the same key string (`actions/cache` with `key: devbin-<project>-<artefact>-<key>`), restored before the build step and saved after it, so a run re-fired on an unchanged key pulls. For a release, the release's own assets are the registry's public face: `release attach` takes an artefact from the registry when its key is R's, and the asset's name carries the key's first twelve characters beside the version. Nothing is fetched from anywhere else: a pull reads the machine's registry or the runner's cache, both written by the same user.

**The verbs.** The core gains `bin/devbin cache`: `key <artefact> [--commit <sha>]` prints the key, or refuses (no `build:` block, an undeclared artefact, a dirty input, an unreadable commit, a line or a sha256 it cannot take, an argument it cannot read) with its reason, a key being held to its form, 64 hex digits, before any path is made from it; `get <artefact> [--commit <sha>]` exits 0 with the artefact at its `path` and the line `pulled <artefact> <key>`, 1 when absent, 7 when refused, the cache's own code in devbin's exit-code contract (2 and 3 stay the dispatcher's: an unknown command, and one nothing here implements); `put <artefact>` records the file at `path` under HEAD's key once the inputs are clean, and refuses a dirty tree with a line and exit 7, so a dirty build runs and leaves no record; `list [<artefact>]`; `rm <key>`; `gc [--keep <n>]` keeps the newest n per artefact (3 unless `--keep` says, `CACHE_GC_KEEP` in the code) and every key the newest RELEASE seal names on a `cache<TAB><artefact><TAB><key>` line, the line a cut writes for each artefact it used (WP02b-2 and WP08 write it; until a seal carries one, `gc` keeps the newest n alone and says no seal named a key), the newest by its time, as runlog's `newest_run_stems` reads every kept run, and refuses, removing nothing, when that seal cannot be read; it prints what went and the bytes freed, and acts only on a name of a key's form. A project's `build` handler calls `get` before its build and `put` after; the core's own `build` command does not change; a `derived:` command may do the same; where the handler is the core's own (WP08's formula, WP06's macOS stage), the core calls them itself. The words follow `ci-state`'s discipline: one line, one word, the reason on refusal, never a silent miss.

**What it removes**, per the record: Intent's pre-push cold clone-and-build pulls whenever the clone's inputs are the working tree's, the common case after a commit; Gtools's re-cut after a red leg and its macOS leg's second build on the same inputs pull; Laksa's second prod compile pulls; Conflab, measured by conflab-dc and checked by conflab-vc at ffdba212 (2026-10-31): its three cargo builds are three distinct artefacts (conflab, conflabd, conflab-stamp) plus Conflab.app, each built once per cut in `after:` 2 after the legs are green, and the stamp step writes VERSION into every one's inputs, so no cut can pull an earlier cut's artefact, and the one same-key repeat, conflab-stamp under `test swift` and again under the app build, is already a cargo no-op; the cache removes no build from Conflab's cut, Conflab declares no `build:` block in WP13, and AC-5.4 does not reach it. What a cache could still save there is the dev loop's cold `fullcycle` restore, on two conditions that are Conflab cc's: one declaration of each artefact's inputs (native/stamp/src/inputs.rs already holds it, so a `build:` block would be a second copy unless derived from it), and `conflab doctor`'s build-versus-HEAD rule moving onto the key, since the key ignores history and a pull after a rebase would read as needing a rebuild. The general lesson holds for every consumer: an artefact whose declared inputs carry a per-cut stamp never hits across cuts, by design; the cache's saving is inside one cut (a re-cut after a red leg, a second leg on the same inputs) and in the dev loop. Gtools's ten cold runner builds stay builds, one per platform per key, and a run re-fired on the same key, the re-cut, pulls from the runner's cache. The measure is WP15's builds-per-release column, before and after.

**An absent cache is a miss, never a failure** (hv's question, 2026-10-31 12:5xZ). `DEVBIN_CACHE_HOME` unset or empty means the default root, `$(xdg_dir cache)/devbin`; nothing has to be set for a build to run. A root that does not exist yet is an empty registry: `get` answers 1, absent, the build runs, and `put` makes the root and the entry (`mkdir -p`), so the first build on a machine fills the cache rather than tripping over it. A root that cannot be used (a relative or non-absolute value, a path that is a file or a link to nothing, one this user cannot write, one that cannot be made because the nearest path above it that exists is not a directory this user can write or is a link to nothing, a disk that is full) makes `get` and `put` say so, one line each on stderr naming the root and the reason, before the key asks the toolchain anything, exit 7, and the build handler goes on; a `put` that stops at any step leaves no temporary entry under the root, and a `get` that cannot write the artefact refuses rather than answer absent: the registry is a cache, its absence costs a build and nothing else, and the line is the whole of what No Silent Errors asks. A `put` that fails after a green build never unmakes the build's exit. On CI the same holds: a restore miss of the runner's cache is a build, and a save that fails is a line in the job's log. `bin/devbin doctor` reports the cache root it resolves, the default marked as such, and whether it can be written, as a note when it cannot, and fails an input path the block declares that HEAD does not hold, so a wrong value is read before a cut rather than in one. The one thing the cache never does is pull on a doubtful entry: a key, manifest or `SHA256SUMS` that does not verify is removed with a line and the build runs.

**Integrity.** A pull verifies `SHA256SUMS` and the manifest's key against the key asked; a mismatch removes the entry with a line and the build runs. A directory is restored by tar with its recorded mode bits and nothing else (no owner, no xattrs, no ACLs, no file flags); a file is copied with its mode and times and no file flags, as a directory's tar records none, since a flag such as uchg or uappnd on the registry's copy would leave an entry nothing could replace or remove. The registry is the user's own and is never shared between users or machines in this design; a fleet registry (one on yggdrasil, or GitHub Packages) is a later decision, taken only if WP15 shows the per-machine cache leaves a build worth removing.

**Not done here**: no remote artefact registry; no cross-platform transfer; no cache for a test suite (D57 is that); no claim of reproducible-build equality between machines; no per-project setup beyond the `build:` block.

**Declared limits** (hv's rulings on I8 and I9 of the critic-shell review of 0c70f300..4774c637, 2026-11-01, relayed by vc, decision 122). The `arch` line is the shell's own `uname -m`, so a build run from an emulated shell, an x86_64 bash under Rosetta on an arm64 Mac, is keyed with the shell's architecture whatever its toolchain builds for: on one machine that is a second key and a miss, never a wrong pull, and a wrong pull would need one registry shared between an emulated shell and a native one, which this design keeps per machine. Every tool but cargo is asked its version at the project root, so a toolchain pinned below it (swiftly's `.swift-version`, asdf's or mise's `.tool-versions`) is not the one the key names; every pin in the fleet sits at its repository's root (12 of 36 repositories carry one, none below it), and a per-artefact `dir:` comes with the first adoption that needs one.

## 1. The step graph

### 1.1 The one sequence, and who runs it

The step names, in order, are written once: `lib/release.steps:94`:

```
_RELEASE_STEP_NAMES=(resolve pre-flight stamp commit gates confirm tag push snapshot candidate publish object after ci)
```

A cut (`bin/devbin release <target>`) runs resolve through push, then either stops (publish.url declared) or runs object, after and ci itself (`lib/cmd/release:674` `cut_run`, `:1183-1206`). `release publish` runs resolve, pre-flight, snapshot, confirm, candidate, publish, then the same object, after and ci through `cut_tail` (`lib/cmd/release:2776` `publish_run`, `:3046-3049`). The real cut and the real publish each run inside one sealed gate of their own: `run_gate --label release --suffix RELEASE ... -- cut_run` (`lib/cmd/release:3346`) and `run_gate --label "release publish" --suffix PUBLISH ... -- publish_run` (`:3326`). A dry run of either is not sealed.

Every step with a postcondition reads it first; the readers live in `lib/release.steps` and `release status` prints the same table through the same readers (`lib/cmd/release:3106` `status_report`). Three steps have no postcondition and run on every run that reaches them: gates ("never already: the gates run on every run until the tag exists", `lib/cmd/release:3175`), after (`:3274`) and ci (`:3281`).

### 1.5 The per-step map in one line, Devbin's current shape

cut: resolve, pre-flight, stamp, commit, [gates: check all; test all; doctor], confirm (prompt), tag, push to `local`, stop. By hand: `release snapshot` to read the sha (optional), then `release publish --expect <sha> --yes`. publish: resolve, pre-flight (public ls-remote), snapshot (fetch public history), confirm, candidate push, wait up to 90m for the matrix, ff main, push tag, delete candidate, wait up to 20m for `release.yml`'s object, run `formula publish` (which cannot ask under `--yes`, so FAILED, exit 1), ci skipped. By hand: `formula publish` at a terminal, `brew upgrade devbin`, `devbin use brew`.
